observation.visible_scene: A clear glass partly filled with water sits on a dark wooden table against a plain light-gray wall. A red-and-white striped colored pencil leans inside the glass, its tip protruding above the rim. The pencil looks visually discontinuous at the water surface (the submerged portion appears shifted relative to the part above water). Several other colored pencils (magenta, white, green on the left; yellow, dark-red, green, blue on the right) lie flat on the table around the glass.
visible_changes: The camera slowly moves closer to / zooms in on the glass over the excerpt: the glass and the leaning pencil grow larger in frame, and the rim and water line rise higher.

Because of this approach, the peripheral table pencils shift outward in the frame (left group toward the left edge, right group toward the right edge), while the glass stays near the horizontal center.
The apparent 'bent' or broken look of the pencil at the air-water interface persists throughout; it is an optical effect of the water, not the pencil physically deforming.
The pencils themselves (the one in the glass and those on the table) show no independent sliding, rolling, or falling; their relative positions on the table remain fixed.
The water level and the meniscus at the surface remain essentially unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the pencil came to rest leaning in the glass, and whether the camera zoom continues past the last frame or stops.
Any motion before the first frame or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Whether the small apparent change in the leaning pencil's angle is due to the camera's changing perspective or an actual tiny rotation/slide of the pencil on the rim.
The exact camera path (pure zoom vs. slight forward translation/tilt) cannot be separated cleanly from the background evidence.
